observation: The whole set in the opening position, all 186 occurrences. Top: the 7x9 field is correct -- twelve cocoa-brown belt tiles in two 2x3 blocks on files b-c and e-f across ranks 4-6, the Sol star at d1 with three orange corona cells at c1, d2, e1, the Anti-Sol star at d9 with three cyan cells at c9, d8, e9, sixteen pieces on their opening cells (eight white discs, eight black), and both trays clear of the board with eight sockets each. The two Mercury pieces are what this round reviews: at board scale they now carry a marking a reader can point at -- a bright white dot inside a brown ring, with brown plains round it on a grey ball -- where the set being corrected showed featureless grey balls at this same scale. Iso: the rank ladder reads at a glance, Mercury smallest and Jupiter and Saturn largest, and Saturn's ring and web are present on both armies, mirrored. Front: every piece stands on the board plane, disc walls draft outward on the white army and inward on the black, and the star flames rise clear and lean outward. Nothing floats, nothing is missing, nothing duplicated, no intersection visible. Two things a reader could mistake for faults: flames and corona tongues stand beside a seated world, never inside one -- measure/seated-piece-clearance.md, regenerated this run, gives 0.000000 mm3 shared on all eight worlds at both seats; and Saturn's ring meets its disc across a shared surface by design, with the whole-assembly interference check left to the verifier run that follows this round. Renderer limits, not geometry: black discs come out as flat silhouettes with no top face, the trays read as floating because nothing is drawn under them, and the numerals face the seated players so they are nearly side-on here.
